items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: I still after work drove into New York, went to Birdland, you know saw Miles, Cannonball, Coltrane, Art Blakey.

ctx.x: I have to write that comment down. “The triad band.” No sevenths allowed.

Yeah exactly. So although I learned that there was a different style of music that drew people, I still after work drove into New York, went to Birdland, you know saw Miles, Cannonball, Coltrane, Art Blakey. And there was also a jazz club in Newark called Sugar Hill and all the great jazz players came in. And I still followed, you know listened to jazz and was sort of drawn to do that. And in 1959 – well after The Four Lovers had their hit record Elvis became popular on RCA and The Four Lovers went on the back…

music. He’d give me a record and say, “Charles I want the rhythm to sound like this. I want the horns to play this style, and I need strings. And here’s what I want the strings to do.” And he’d give me records to listen to.
